question: What are the three distinct phases that make up the peri-operative continuum?
explanation: Peri-operative care is structurally divided into the pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative phases to ensure comprehensive patient safety throughout the surgical journey. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is the peri-operative period viewed as a single continuous continuum rather than three isolated events?

options.A: A lapse in safety measures during one phase directly impacts outcomes in subsequent phases.
options.B: The same individual nurse must remain with the patient for the entire duration.
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards require surgical notes to be filed as a single document.
options.D: Patients are kept under continuous general anaesthesia from admission to discharge.

explanation: Because each phase heavily relies on the preceding one, continuous and coordinated nursing care prevents complications from carrying over into recovery. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is a primary objective of the pre-operative nursing assessment?

options.A: Determining the exact cost of the surgical procedure for the family
options.B: Performing the surgical scrub and draping the patient's skin
options.C: Administering the final dose of general anaesthesia in the ward
options.D: Establishing a baseline of the patient's physiological and psychological status

explanation: Baseline assessments provide crucial comparative data for detecting complications during and after the surgical procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for an elective hernia repair expresses deep fear about dying on the operating table. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Immediately administer a strong sedative without waiting for a doctor's order.
options.B: Dismiss the worry by explaining that hernia repairs are minor, routine surgeries.
options.C: Tell the patient that worrying will only cause blood pressure to rise.
options.D: Acknowledge the fear and offer an opportunity for the patient to talk about their concerns.

explanation: Psychological preparation involves validating patient anxiety and providing supportive communication rather than dismissing valid fears. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which duty is specifically assigned to the circulating nurse rather than the scrub nurse?

options.A: Performing the surgical hand scrub and donning a sterile gown
options.B: Handling sterile instruments directly to the operating surgeon
options.C: Managing the overall unsterile environment and documenting events
options.D: Maintaining the sterile field right beside the surgical incision

explanation: The circulating nurse operates in the unsterile field to manage room logistics, patient safety, and documentation, while the scrub nurse stays sterile. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: During a laparotomy, the circulating nurse notices that a packet of gauze sponges was opened but not recorded on the count board. What is the correct immediate action?

options.A: Ignore the missing record since sponges are usually accounted for at the end.
options.B: Tell the scrub nurse to throw away any loose sponges found on the floor.
options.C: Ask the surgeon to rush the final closure so the discrepancy can be checked later.
options.D: Pause the procedure to reconcile the count with the scrub nurse before wound closure proceeds.

explanation: Immediate reconciliation of surgical items prevents retained foreign objects, a critical intra-operative safety standard. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care immediately upon admitting a patient to the recovery room?

options.A: Removing all intravenous lines and wound drainage tubes
options.B: Maintaining a patent airway and monitoring respiratory status
options.C: Arranging immediate transfer back to the general surgical ward
options.D: Serving heavy meals to restore the patient's nutritional balance

explanation: Airway patency and adequate ventilation are the top priorities during the immediate post-operative period due to residual anaesthetic effects. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h4)

question: What clinical purpose does scoring systems like the Aldrete score serve in the recovery unit?

options.A: Calculating the financial cost of medications used during surgery
options.B: Diagnosing the underlying pathology that necessitated the operation
options.C: Determining safe readiness for discharge from the recovery room
options.D: Evaluating the competency of the surgeon who performed the procedure

explanation: Scoring tools provide objective physiological criteria to confirm whether a patient has recovered sufficiently from anaesthesia to leave the recovery area. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h4)

question: At what exact point in the surgical journey is the WHO 'Time Out' pause performed?

options.A: Immediately before skin incision is made
options.B: When the patient is first admitted to the ward
options.C: After the patient has been discharged home
options.D: During the initial pre-operative clinic visit

explanation: The Time Out serves as a final collective verification pause right before the incision to prevent wrong-site or wrong-patient errors. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why is active multidisciplinary participation encouraged during surgical safety checklist verification?

options.A: It empowers every team member to speak up and prevents hierarchical communication barriers.
options.B: It allows the scrub nurse to take over anaesthetic responsibilities.
options.C: It ensures that the hospital management board can review staff attendance rates.
options.D: It replaces the need for keeping formal written nursing care plans.

explanation: Checklists work best when all team members share accountability and communicate openly, regardless of professional rank. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h5)

question: A surgeon asks the ward nurse to obtain a patient's signature on a consent form after the patient has already received preoperative oral diazepam. What is the correct nursing response?

options.A: Ask the anaesthetist to administer an antidote so the patient can sign safely.
options.B: Sign the form on behalf of the patient to save time for the theatre schedule.
options.C: Proceed to get the signature quickly since a family member is present to witness it.
options.D: Refuse to obtain the signature because the sedative impairs legal capacity for informed consent.

explanation: Informed consent obtained after the administration of mind-altering medications is legally invalid because the patient's capacity is compromised. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following describes the legal standard for peri-operative nursing documentation? (Choose the best answer)

options.A: Verbal agreements documented from memory the next day
options.B: General summaries written at the end of the weekly shift
options.C: Contemporaneous, objective, and accurate records of care
options.D: Subjective personal opinions regarding patient compliance

explanation: Documentation must be done in real time (contemporaneously) and focus on factual, objective observations rather than personal opinions. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h6)
